name: Gildmoss Crest (original)
change: The chosen round 1 direction, shown first for comparison.

name: Gildmoss Bare
change: No gold rim on panels: polished glass bevel edges, small engraved corner caps and a slim clasp where panels join.
good: Directly tests your 'panels without a gold border' idea; the lightest, most modern of the five; the glass reads as the material and the world shows through more.
watch: Without a rim, panels lean on the corner caps for definition; over a bright, busy scene the edge is softer.

name: Gildmoss Etched
change: Same hairline rim plus a faint frosted reed-and-leaf band etched into the glass just inside it.
good: Adds texture and a riverside motif with no extra metal; the etching reads as part of the glass, not as a border.
watch: The etched band sits close to text margins; it must stay this faint, and it disappears at small sizes.

name: Gildmoss Notched
change: Corners carry small angled champagne corner plates, and connected panels are joined by a slim spine with a roundel.
good: Gives the panels a more game-like silhouette at the corners and the clearest joint between the HUD and the Journal.
watch: The notch came out subtle: the corners read as small corner plates rather than cut-away corners.

name: Gildmoss Lantern
change: A small lantern-bracket crest at the centre of each panel's top edge, with the lantern light spreading from it.
good: Gives each panel a clear 'top' and a source for the lantern light you asked for more of; the crest is small enough to stay out of the way.
watch: The model put the lantern crest only on the HUD, not the Journal, and added a bright glint at the joint between them that reads as a light leak.

name: Gildmoss Filigree
change: Fine pierced leaf-scroll filigree at the corners, a thin double hairline rim and a filigree clasp between panels.
good: The richest of the five while staying calm behind text; the leaf scrolls feel crafted rather than stamped; the double rim and filigree clasp read well together.
watch: Corner filigree at every panel adds up quickly; small buttons get crowded corners, as in the kit's button row.

name: Corner Mount
change: A sculpted corner piece fills the screen corner with gilded rails along the top and left edges; the round portrait medallion sits in it, with tapered plates for the needs and statuses.
good: Looks built into the screen frame, exactly the embedded feeling; tapered plates keep the bars long and readable; the lock toggle docks onto the portrait ring.
watch: The left-edge rail runs about 40% of the screen height, which may be more than you want; it could stop much higher.

name: Ringed Dial
change: The needs become concentric arcs around the portrait ring, like the rings of an astrolabe, with statuses set in sockets along the outer arc.
good: The most distinctive silhouette: the needs sweep out of the portrait like the rings of an astrolabe; the portrait is the centrepiece and large enough to show the pixel art.
watch: Curved arcs make it harder to compare how full each need is; the eye toggle sits at the end of the arcs where it reads as a fifth need.

name: Escutcheon
change: The portrait sits in a heraldic shield with a crest; needs and statuses ride on rigid glass pennants fixed to the shield.
good: Heraldic and medieval at a glance; the long pennants keep the bars straight and easy to compare; the shield's crest gives the corner a strong silhouette.
watch: Reads as noble or knightly heraldry, more than a survivor's camp; the swallowtail ends add width.

name: Lantern Window
change: The portrait sits in a pointed-arch lantern pane hanging from a gilded bracket on the top screen edge; needs and statuses hang beside it.
good: Most directly 'hung in the screen corner' from a bracket; the lantern cap lights the portrait, tying into the lantern-light preference; the hanging eye toggle is charming.
watch: The rectangular plates beside the arch are the least unique part; the gilded bracket along the top edge makes the corner feel heavy.

name: Reedscroll
change: One continuous cast housing: the portrait ring flows into a curved cradle for the needs, with reed-stem flourishes along the screen edges.
good: One continuous cast piece, so it reads most like a single crafted object; reed and leaf flourishes tie it to the riverside setting; the most compact for its content.
watch: Leaf flourishes spill down the left edge and could crowd other UI there; the eye toggle floats separately at the right end.
